original_record.question:
The diagram (which is not drawn to scale) shows a box measuring $5 \mathrm{~cm}$ by $5 \mathrm{~cm}$. There are seven bars in the box, each measuring $1 \mathrm{~cm}$ by $3 \mathrm{~cm}$. Kanga wants to slide the bars in the box so there is room for one more bar. What is the minimum number of bars that Kanga needs to move?

<image1>
original_record.solution: Label three of the bars $\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}$ and $\mathrm{Z}$ as shown in the diagram. At the start Kanga can only move bar X down. Now Y and $\mathrm{Z}$ are the only bars that can be moved and Kanga must slide these bars to the left. Only now is there space for one more bar and Kanga has moved 3 bars.  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-113.jpg?height=311&width=305&top_left_y=852&top_left_x=1502)
